# TOOTH ABSCESS AND OTHER SUPPURATIVE ODONTOGENIC INFECTIONS Surgical drainage, scaling and antimicrobial treatment are essential and tooth extraction is required in most cases. All patients should be referred to the dental service for assessment and direction of treatment. Empirical coverage for likely pathogens (streptococci, Peptostreptococcus, Finegoldia, Bacteriodes and other oral anaerobes is required. Immunocompromised patients need additional coverage for Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

## Consult Dental Service.

---

Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Preferred:

Treatment of mild to moderate disease in immunocompetent patients or step-down therapy after initial intravenous therapy. Adjust duration for a total of 7-14 days of antimicrobial therapy.
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h for 7 to 14 days ($) [R]
Alternative
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Clindamycin 450 mg PO q8h for 7 to 14 days ($) [H,O]
Treatment of severe disease in immunocompetent patients
Preferred:
Ampicillin-sulbactam 3gm IV q6h for 7 to 14 days ($) [R]
Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Ceftriaxone 1 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q6h ($) [DI] for 7 to 14 days
Treatment in immunocompromised patients
Preferred:
Cefepime 2g IV q12h ($$) [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) [DI]
< OR >
Ceftazidime 2 gm IV q8h ($$) [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) [DI]
Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h ($) [R] for 5 days

### Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

Azithromycin 500 mg PO once on day one then 250mg PO qday for 4 days ($) [M]

*Local guidance (Des Moines CDSS, Inpatient):*
Meropenem 1 gm IV q8h for 7 to 14 days ($$) [R,O]

## ER/UC

Surgical drainage, scaling and antimicrobial treatment are essential and tooth extraction is required in most cases. All patients should be referred to the dental service for assessment and direction of treatment. Empirical coverage for likely pathogens (streptococci, Peptostreptococcus, Finegoldia, Bacteriodes and other oral anaerobes is required. Immunocompromised patients need additional coverage for Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

### Treatment of mild to moderate disease in immunocompetent patients or step-down therapy after initial intravenous therapy. Adjust duration for a total of 7-14 days of antimicrobial therapy.

Preferred:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h for 7 to 14 days ($) [R]

Alternative:
Clindamycin 450 mg PO q8h for 7 to 14 days ($) [H,O]

### Treatment of severe disease in immunocompetent patients

Preferred:
Ampicillin-sulbactam 3gm IV once STAT ($) [R]

Alternative:
Ceftriaxone 1 gm IV once STAT ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT ($) [DI]

### Treatment in immunocompromised patients

Preferred:
Cefepime 2 g IV once STAT ($$) [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT ($) [DI]
<OR>
Ceftazidime 2 gm IV once STAT ($$) [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT ($) [DI]

Alternative:
Meropenem 1 gm IV once STAT ($$) [R,O]
ERUC: ORZID GMENU ER/UC SUPP ODONTOGENIC INFECT
